- Dark green powdery mold growing on kernels and between husks
- Mold appears to cover a broad area of the ear surface
- The color is distinctly dark green/teal, not olive-green or pink

Top candidates: **Ear_rots_Trichoderma** (dark green mold) or **Ear_rots_Aspergillus** (olive-green/gray-green). Let me view references for both, plus a few others to confirm.
The Trichoderma reference matches extremely well — dark green/teal mold between kernels and on husks, exactly as seen in the test image. Let me check a few more to be thorough.
None of those match — Gibberella shows pink-red/brown, Diplodia shows white/tan, Fusarium shows white/pink. Let me view more to reach the 12-image minimum.

All other leaf diseases (Gray leaf spot, NCLB, Common rust, Tar spot, Southern rust, Goss's wilt, Stewart's wilt) are clearly leaf-based diseases — not relevant to an ear rot case.

**Summary of evidence:**

| Feature | Test Image | Trichoderma | Aspergillus |
|---------|-----------|-------------|-------------|
| Color | Dark green/teal | ✅ Dark green | ❌ Olive/gray-green dusty |
| Location | Kernels + husks | ✅ Kernels + between | ❌ Typically tip |
| Coverage | Broad/scattered | ✅ Often covers entire ear | ❌ Usually localized |
